Provinces were sampled with reference, oversampling, and Canada-level participation; Saskatchewan and Manitoba are treated as Canada-level only, while other provinces are reported individually (reference and oversampled).

data.outcome_summary: This CMEC report summarizes PIRLS 2011 reading outcomes for Canada and participating provinces (4th-year students), using the PIRLS reading scale (0–1000, with an international center point at 500) and reporting 95% confidence intervals. It describes the assessment design: two 40-minute test sessions with multiple-choice and constructed-response items across 10 reading passages (50% literary, 50% informational), plus a 30-minute student questionnaire and additional parent/teacher/school questionnaires. Results are presented by overall reading performance, by reading purpose (literary vs informational), by comprehension processes (extract/infer vs interpret/combine/evaluate), by sex, and by international benchmarks (advanced, high, intermediate, low) with benchmark attainment percentages. The report also documents contextual patterns: students who speak the test language at home, whose parents frequently engage in early literacy activities, and who show positive reading attitudes tend to have higher reading scores, while excessive homework time and frequent bullying are associated with lower performance. No machine-learning model is trained or evaluated; the findings are descriptive and benchmark-based, so causal claims are not established.
